title: High-resolution mapping of reciprocal translocation breakpoints using long-read sequencing
author: Chow, Cheng, et al.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from blood
steps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA from peripheral blood using the QIAamp DNA Blood Mini kit (Qiagen, Manchester, UK).

steps.title: Verify DNA integrity by gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Assess the extracted DNA quality by running an aliquot on an agarose gel electrophoresis and confirm high‑molecular‑weight DNA.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing library with 1 µg DNA
steps.instruction: Take exactly 1 µg of the verified DNA and construct a sequencing library using the SQK‑LSK108 kit (Oxford Nanopore, Oxford, UK) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Run MinION sequencing (48 h)
steps.instruction: Load the prepared library onto a MinION flow cell (R9.4, Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK) and initiate the standard 48‑hour sequencing run.

substeps.instruction: Prime the flow cell as instructed by ONT.
Load the library onto the flow cell.
Start the 48‑hour sequencing protocol using the MinKNOW software.

steps.title: Perform local base calling
steps.instruction: Execute local base‑calling on the raw MinION signal data using the appropriate ONT base‑calling software (e.g., Guppy).

steps.title: Align reads and identify breakpoints
steps.instruction: Align the base‑called reads to the reference genome, then analyze the alignments to determine the reciprocal translocation breakpoints.

substeps.instruction: Use a suitable aligner (e.g., Minimap2) for long‑read mapping.
Inspect split‑read and discordant alignments to locate breakpoint coordinates.

steps.title: Confirm breakpoints via Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Design primers flanking the predicted breakpoint regions and validate the breakpoints by Sanger sequencing of the PCR products.
